specification.family_title: Commit outcome after a connection or reply failure
specification.title: The connection is terminated after the last write, before COMMIT
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(). The runner terminates that backend from its own connection, and waits until it has gone.
Wait settle_ms, so that the driver can observe the closed connection.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework attempts to commit.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When the connection or PostgreSQL's reply was lost around COMMIT, so that the client never received an acknowledgement of COMMIT, the API does not report a successful commit.

execution.description: DriverManagerDataSource. A connection is opened for the transaction and closed when Spring releases it. No pool. The outer TransactionTemplate uses the default PROPAGATION_REQUIRED. A nested TransactionTemplate uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. TX-03 is not run in this mode (not-applicable-by-design). On this server, DataSourceUtils.releaseConnection closed a connection whose autocommit was false, and that backend was gone from pg_stat_activity. DataSourceTransactionManager.doCleanupAfterCompletion unbinds the holder and then calls releaseConnection, which closes the connection because it is no longer bound. The next TransactionTemplate ran on a different backend. This DataSource cannot hand a transactionally active connection to later work.
execution.form: TransactionTemplate with the default PROPAGATION_REQUIRED on DataSourceTransactionManager. Writes go through JdbcTemplate.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: pg_terminate_backend(pid), run by the runner from its own connection.
fault.injection_point: After the last write, before the framework sends COMMIT.
fault.preconditions: The PID the adapter reports belongs to the case's database.
fault.expected_server: The backend exits, and its transaction is rolled back.
fault.expected_client: A connection error at COMMIT. No reply to COMMIT can arrive.

knowledge: Known not committed: the session ended before the framework tried to commit, so the driver refused to send COMMIT ("Client has encountered a connection error and is not queryable"). A report of rollback is justified; a report of success is not.

api_outcome.basis: TransactionTemplate.execute threw an exception the callback did not throw
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute (org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate) calls PlatformTransactionManager.commit only when the callback returns, and on a RuntimeException or Error it rolls the transaction back and rethrows that same throwable. The 7.0.9 reference, Rolling Back a Declarative Transaction, states the default rule: "In its default configuration, the Spring Framework's transaction infrastructure code marks a transaction for rollback only in the case of runtime, unchecked exceptions. That is, when the thrown exception is an instance or subclass of RuntimeException. (Error instances also, by default, result in a rollback)." The default tx:advice settings say: "Any RuntimeException triggers rollback, and any checked Exception does not." No custom rollback rule is installed. The nested TransactionTemplate uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. The 7.0.9 reference, Understanding PROPAGATION_NESTED, states: "PROPAGATION_NESTED uses a single physical transaction with multiple savepoints that it can roll back to. Such partial rollbacks let an inner transaction scope trigger a rollback for its scope, with the outer transaction being able to continue the physical transaction despite some operations having been rolled back. This setting is typically mapped onto JDBC savepoints, so it works only with JDBC resource transactions." DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc states: "This transaction manager supports nested transactions via the JDBC Savepoint mechanism."
